newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen down, but $2,000 support firm.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen down, but $2,000 support firm.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
London robusta coffee futures were called $100 a tonne lower on Thursday after New York's nearby coffee stumbled on Colombian news.
Chartwise, the second-month September contract could slide towards the closely-watched $2,000 but analysts said the support level seemed intact.
Traders said in practice, coffee could fall by $50-$60 a tonne.
Adrian Haylor, an analyst at Sucden, said the $2,000 mark on September was a pretty big support.
Immediately, the market could test $2,040 support before challenging the major $2,000 mark.
"A break below $2,000 will expose the chart gap at $1,940 and $1,973 and then the 40-day moving average at $1,854," he said.
This could take the market further down at $1,750.
On the upside, the big chart gap at $2,305 and $2,500 would offer a major hurdle.
The 14-day relative strength indicator was at a neutral 54 percent as the market underwent a sharp technical correction to the recent overbought conditions.
Colombia said this week it would open unlimited coffee sales for July and August. The news dragged both London and New York sharply lower on Wednesday.
The government and the Coffee Growers Federation had anticipated no more than about 2.5 million bags would be available for shipment during the period.
Broker GNI said while fresh supplies were likely to be limited, the sales would probably be boosted by old crop stock drawdown.

On the weather front, forecasters said cooling temperatures to between below and well below normal levels were predicted for Brazil's coffee growing regions over this weekend but no damaging cold was expected.
